title: Brussels sprouts, frozen, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Brussels sprouts are small cabbage-like heads harvested as compact buds. This product is frozen, pre‑cooked sprouts with no added fat. Rapid freezing after harvest locks in nutrients and flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vegetable is named after Brussels, where it was first cultivated in the 16th century.
One serving (100 g) provides about 43 kcal, making it a low‑calorie food.
Sprouts are rich in glucoraphanin, a compound that supports gut health.
Freezing preserves the bright green color and a crisp texture after reheating.
Brussels sprouts belong to the cruciferous family, along with broccoli and cauliflower.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and acts as a powerful antioxidant.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate supports DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: No added fat makes this product suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to cabbage family vegetables.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Compounds in sprouts can cause bloating or gas in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Glucoraphanin content
items.content: Large amounts may cause gastrointestinal discomfort for some people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen sprouts by steaming, microwaving, or sautéing without oil. They can be added to salads, soups, stews, or served as a side dish with meat or fish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, consume within 1–2 days and do not re‑freeze; refrigerated leftovers should be used within 24 hours.
